32.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Old Testament, during the patriarchal period, where lineages and inheritances are of paramount importance for the people of Israel.
32.passage: This verse is part of a genealogy that traces the descendants of Abraham, highlighting the importance of each son in the divine plan. It shows how God's promise to Abraham extends beyond the sole lineage of Isaac.
32.culture: In Hebrew culture, genealogies were essential for establishing identity and legitimacy. They also served to remind of God's promises and the role of each individual in sacred history.
32.interpretation: Spiritually, this verse teaches us that God uses all our relationships and experiences to fulfill His plan. Even the descendants of a concubine are included in the redemption narrative, showing that God's grace knows no bounds.
32.commentaire: This passage reminds us that every person has a place in God's plan, regardless of their origin. It encourages us to recognize and celebrate the diversity of God's family while remaining faithful to our calling. As believers, we are called to be instruments of peace and blessing in the world, just like the descendants of Abraham.

mots.sens: The term 'Midian' refers both to a people and a geographical region. Historically, the Midianites were often in conflict with the Israelites, but they also played a role in the history of God's people. Spiritually, Midian sometimes symbolizes the struggle between faith and external influences, reminding believers of the importance of remaining faithful to God despite the temptations of the world.

Keturah, whose name means 'incense', is Abraham's second wife, representing a continuity of the divine promise beyond Isaac's lineage. She illustrates Abraham's faithfulness to God, even in his family relationships, and emphasizes that God's blessings can extend to other lineages. Spiritually, this reminds us that God uses various paths to accomplish His purposes.

The word 'sons' (בָּנִים) evokes not only physical descent but also spiritual heritage. In biblical culture, sons are often seen as bearers of the divine promise and continuators of the faith. This teaches us about our identity in Christ, where every believer is called to be an heir of God's promises.

33.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the history of Israel, after the death of Abraham, during a period when tribes and lineages are being established. It is a time of transition where Abraham's descendants begin to multiply and disperse.
33.passage: In this chapter, the author of 1 Chronicles outlines a genealogical tree of Abraham's descendants, highlighting the importance of lineages in the divine plan. This verse specifies the descendants of Keturah, emphasizing that even the children from a secondary union have their place in the history of salvation.
33.culture: In ancient culture, genealogy was crucial for establishing a person's identity and status. The descendants of Abraham, whether from Sarah or Keturah, had specific roles in the history of Israel and in God's promise.
33.interpretation: This verse reminds us that God's promise is not limited to a single lineage but extends to all those connected to Abraham. It emphasizes the inclusivity of God's plan for humanity, where every individual has value and purpose in the kingdom of God.
33.commentaire: The study of this verse invites us to reflect on our own spiritual heritage in Christ. Just as the sons of Keturah were integrated into the biblical narrative, we are called to be part of God's story through our faith. This encourages us to live in a way that honors our spiritual heritage and to pass on the faith to future generations.

mots.sens: The name 'Avraham' means 'father of a multitude'. It is derived from the Hebrew root 'רָהָם' which evokes the idea of growth and promise. In this verse, Abraham is presented as the founding patriarch of the people of Israel, highlighting the theological significance of the divine promise made to him and his descendants.

The name 'Yitzhak' means 'he will laugh', evoking joy and the fulfillment of God's promises. Derived from the root 'צָחַק', it also symbolizes faith and trust in God, even in the face of impossible circumstances. In this verse, Isaac is the son of the promise, representing the continuity of the divine covenants.

The name 'Esav' means 'made' or 'complete', which may refer to his birth, where he is described as 'red and hairy'. This word is related to the notion of the flesh and earthly desires. In the context of this verse, Esav represents the spiritual challenges that Abraham's descendants will have to face.

The name 'Yisraël' means 'he who struggles with God'. It is derived from the roots 'שָׂרָה' (to struggle) and 'אֵל' (God). In this verse, Israel is the name given to Jacob, symbolizing the intimate relationship between God and His people, as well as the call to spiritual struggle and faithfulness to divine promises.

34.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Old Testament, during a time when the patriarchs were establishing the foundations of the nation of Israel, marking the history of redemption.
34.passage: 1 Chronicles 1:34 is part of a genealogy that traces the origins of the people of Israel, emphasizing the importance of the ancestors in God's divine plan of salvation.
34.culture: In Hebrew culture, genealogies are essential for establishing the identity and legitimacy of clans and tribes. They bear witness to God's faithfulness to His promises.
34.interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity of God's covenant through the generations, shedding light on the two sons of Isaac, Esau and Israel, who represent opposing spiritual choices. It reminds us that each generation must face choices that will determine their relationship with God.
34.commentaire: The verse reminds us of the importance of God's promises through the generations. As believers, we are called to walk in the faith of Abraham and to recognize our identity in Christ, heirs of the promises. This passage encourages us to choose the path of faithfulness, like Israel, rather than that of earthly desires, like Esau.

mots.sens: The name Esau means 'red' or 'hairy', which refers to his appearance at birth. Esau is the son of Isaac and the twin brother of Jacob, representing a lineage that, although often in conflict with Jacob's, plays a crucial role in the history of Israel. Spiritually, Esau symbolizes life choices that can lead to the loss of divine blessings, highlighting the importance of faithfulness to God.

The name Eliphaz means 'my God is gold', which can be interpreted as a reference to wealth or prosperity. Eliphaz is the firstborn of Esau and represents the continuity of the Edomite lineage. Theologically, his name may remind us that material wealth should never replace an authentic relationship with God.

Reuel means 'friend of God', which emphasizes a potential spiritual connection. As the son of Esau, he represents a bridge between the nations and the people of God. This evokes the idea that even those who are not directly in the lineage of Israel can have a relationship with the God of Israel, highlighting the universality of divine grace.

The name Koré can be linked to notions of 'gathering' or 'assembly'. In the context of Esau, this could symbolize the importance of community and family relationships. Spiritually, it reminds us that our choices and actions influence not only our lives but also those of our family and community.

35.epoque: This passage is set in a historical context where the descendants of Esau, the Edomites, have a complex relationship with the Israelites, reflecting the tensions between these two nations throughout biblical history.
35.passage: 1 Chronicles 1 traces the genealogy of the descendants of Esau, highlighting the importance of lineage in the history of Israel. This chapter aims to establish the roots and identity of the people of God by linking them to their ancestors.
35.culture: In Hebrew culture, genealogy was essential for establishing rights of inheritance and tribal identities. Names often carried deep meanings and spiritual implications, reflecting the relationship between the name and the character of the person.
35.interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity of Esau's lineage while reminding us that each person's spiritual choices can influence their heritage. The names of Esau's sons carry meanings that invite us to reflect on our own relationship with God and our spiritual heritage.
35.commentaire: This passage reminds us of the importance of our roots and spiritual heritage. By considering the names and their meanings, we are encouraged to reflect on our own identity in Christ and how our choices can influence future generations. Let us be faithful heirs of God's grace, seeking to honor our spiritual heritage.

mots.sens: This name means 'God is gold' and represents an important lineage in the genealogy of Esau. Eliphaz is often associated with wisdom and wealth, underscoring the importance of divine blessing in the prosperity of his descendants. In the context of this verse, he symbolizes the continuity of God's promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, through the generations.

Amalek is the name of a nation often in conflict with Israel, symbolizing opposition to the will of God. The name is derived from the root that evokes struggle and war, thus reflecting the belligerent nature of this lineage. Spiritually, Amalek represents the forces that oppose the people of God and His plan of redemption.

Théman is a name that means 'the south' or 'the land of the south', often associated with a specific geographical region. It also evokes the idea of warmth and prosperity, suggesting a fertile and rich land. In the biblical context, Théman can symbolize the blessings that accompany those who follow God's path.

Thimna, whose name means 'the portion' or 'the share', can be interpreted as a reference to a person who has a specific place or role in the lineage. This name underscores the importance of each individual in the divine plan, reminding us that everyone has a part in the story of redemption.

36.epoque: This passage is set in a post-exilic period where the Israelites seek to establish their identity and heritage through their ancestors.
36.passage: In 1 Chronicles 1, the chapter presents the genealogy of Israel, highlighting the descendants of Esau and their importance in the history of the people of God.
36.culture: Genealogy was essential in Israelite culture, as it allowed for the claiming of rights, inheritances, and a collective identity within the people of God.
36.interpretation: This verse reminds us that even names often overlooked in the Bible have profound significance and a place in the divine plan. The descendants of Eliphaz, although often associated with conflicts, illustrate the complexity of human and spiritual relationships.
36.commentaire: The study of this verse encourages us to recognize that each generation has a role to play in God's plan. Even in lineages that seem obscure or conflictual, God works to fulfill His promises. This reminds us that our spiritual heritage is precious and that we are called to walk in the light of divine truth.

mots.sens: The name Reuel means 'friend of God' or 'God is a friend.' This name evokes an intimate and privileged relationship with the divine, highlighting the importance of communion with God in the lives of believers. In the context of genealogy, Reuel is an ancestor who plays a significant role in the history of the people of Israel, reminding us that each generation contributes to God's work.

Nahath means 'rest' or 'tranquility.' This term evokes the idea of peace and respite, which is essential in spiritual life. In the biblical context, it can symbolize the peace that God grants to those who walk in His ways, reminding us of the importance of seeking rest in Christ.

Zérach means 'rising of the sun' or 'to shine.' This word is often associated with light and divine revelation. In the context of genealogy, it can symbolize hope and the promise of new beginnings, emphasizing that each generation can bring new light into God's plan.

Schamma means 'to hear' or 'to listen.' This term is related to the idea of receptivity to the word of God. In the context of this verse, it reminds us of the importance of listening to God's voice in our lives, as obedience to His word is essential for living according to His will.

37.epoque: This passage is situated in a period of Israel's history where genealogies are established to show the heritage and identity of God's people, particularly after the exile to Babylon.
37.passage: 1 Chronicles 1 presents a genealogy that traces the origins of the various tribes of Israel, highlighting the importance of lineage and spiritual heritage in understanding the history of the chosen people.
37.culture: In Hebrew culture, genealogies were crucial for establishing inheritance rights and tribal identities. They also served to remind of God's promises through the generations.
37.interpretation: This verse, although it seems simple, emphasizes the importance of family ties and spiritual heritage. Each name mentioned represents a story, a promise, and a call to live in accordance with God's will.
37.commentaire: The study of this verse reminds us that each generation has a role to play in God's plan. As believers, we are called to honor our spiritual heritage while passing on our faith to future generations. This encourages us to be attentive to God's voice and to live in the peace He offers, while being bearers of light in this world.

mots.sens: The word 'Séir' means 'hairy' or 'shaggy,' and it is often associated with a mountain in Edom. This term evokes a wild and untamed nature, representing a people who lived in arid regions. Theologically, Séir also symbolizes opposition to Israel, reminding us that God has a plan for every nation, even those that seem far from Him.

The name 'Lothan' can be interpreted as 'a man who rises' or 'a man of strength.' This word evokes the idea of resilience and strength in the face of challenges. In the biblical context, Lothan could represent those who stand firm in faith, even in difficult times.

The name 'Schobal' means 'one who bears a burden' or 'one who brings goods.' This can symbolize the role of support and responsibility within a community. Spiritually, it reminds us of the importance of bearing one another's burdens and contributing to the collective well-being.

The name 'Ana' means 'to answer' or 'to respond to a call.' This word can be associated with the notion of receptivity and listening. Spiritually, it invites us to be attentive to God's call in our lives and to respond with faith and obedience.

38.epoque: This passage is situated in the historical context of the Old Testament, at a time when the tribes of Israel and their neighbors were in constant interaction, often in conflict or alliance.
38.passage: 1 Chronicles 1 is part of a genealogy that traces the descendants of Adam to Israel, highlighting the importance of lineages in the history of salvation. This chapter establishes the roots of the peoples and their relationship with the people of God.
38.culture: In ancient culture, genealogies were crucial for establishing identity and social status. They served to remind of God's promises to the ancestors and to affirm the spiritual heritage of the descendants.
38.interpretation: This verse, although it seems to simply list names, reminds us that each individual has a place in God's divine plan. The descendants of Séir, although strangers to Israel, are included in the story of humanity that God guides.
38.commentaire: The list of descendants of Séir teaches us that God knows each of us by name and has created us with a purpose. As believers, we are called to remember that our identity in Christ is more important than our earthly heritage. This encourages us to live in a way that honors our divine calling and to bear one another's burdens in our community.

mots.sens: The name 'Lothan' is derived from a root that can mean 'to hide' or 'to be concealed.' In the biblical context, it evokes a connection with descendants who have significance in the genealogy of Esau, thus highlighting familial and tribal relationships. Spiritually, it may remind us that even those who seem less prominent in the story of redemption have a role in God's plan.

The name 'Timna' is associated with a root that means 'a portion' or 'a share.' She is mentioned as the sister of Lothan, which underscores the importance of women in biblical lineages. Spiritually, it may remind us that every person, regardless of their role, has value in the divine plan and that family relationships are essential in the history of faith.

The name 'Hori' is derived from the root 'hor,' which can mean 'mountain.' This can evoke characteristics of strength and stability. In the context of Esau's descendants, it emphasizes the importance of lineages in establishing tribes and nations, and reminds us that God uses people from all backgrounds to fulfill His purposes.

The name 'Homam' is less common, but it can be related to meanings of warmth or human warmth. This can evoke aspects of family life and interpersonal relationships. Spiritually, it may remind us that love and human warmth are essential in our interactions, reflecting God's love for His people.

39.epoque: This passage is situated in the context of the patriarchal period, where genealogies are essential for establishing the identity of the tribes of Israel and their heritage. This occurs after the time of the patriarchs, in a context where the promised land is already in view.
39.passage: 1 Chronicles 1 presents a detailed genealogy, highlighting the importance of lineages and the descendants of Esau. This chapter sheds light on family relationships and the tribes that emerge from these ancestors.
39.culture: In Hebrew culture, genealogies are crucial for establishing inheritance rights and tribal identities. Women, although often less mentioned, play a vital role in the continuity of lineages.
39.interpretation: This verse reminds us that every person, whether mentioned as a descendant or as a family member, has a role in God's grand narrative. Family relationships reflect the community that God desires to establish among His people.
39.commentaire: This passage teaches us the importance of family relationships and spiritual heritage. By recognizing and honoring our ancestors, we can better understand our place in God's plan. Furthermore, it encourages us to build strong and loving relationships within our own families, thus reflecting Christ's love in our lives.

mots.sens: The name 'Shobal' means 'he who is raised' or 'he who is freed.' This term is related to the idea of deliverance and protection, evoking a family leader who guides and protects his own. In the context of genealogy, it represents an important lineage, highlighting God's faithfulness to His promises to His people.

The name 'Aljan' can be interpreted as 'the Lord is exalted' or 'master.' This word evokes the greatness and divine sovereignty. In the context of Shobal's lineage, it reminds us that each generation is under God's authority, who raises and guides His people throughout history.

The term 'Ébal' can mean 'a man of value' or 'a man of strength.' It evokes qualities of bravery and strong character. In the context of genealogy, this name emphasizes the importance of values and character traits that are passed down from generation to generation, reinforcing the idea that God uses men and women of faith to accomplish His purposes.

The name 'Ana' means 'to answer' or 'to reveal.' In the biblical context, this can indicate a response to a prayer or a divine revelation. The mention of this name in the lineage of Zibeon reminds us that God is always listening to His people and that He reveals Himself to those who seek His face.

40.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the time of the kings of Israel, where genealogies were essential for establishing property rights and inheritances. It is a period when lineage and tribal identity were crucial for the survival and cohesion of the people of Israel.
40.passage: 1 Chronicles 1 presents a genealogy tracing the descendants of Adam to David, highlighting the importance of lineages in God's plan. This chapter establishes the foundations of Israel's history and reminds us that each person has a role in the divine purpose.
40.culture: In Hebrew culture, genealogy was a means of preserving national and spiritual identity. Names often carried deep meanings, reflecting the characteristics of individuals and their relationship with God.
40.interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity of God's promise through the generations. Each name mentioned represents not only a person but also a spiritual heritage and a responsibility toward God and the community.
40.commentaire: The genealogy in 1 Chronicles 1:40 reminds us that God works through generations and that each believer is called to play a role in His plan. As we reflect on these names, we can question the legacy we leave and how we live out our faith daily. May our lives be a testimony to God's greatness, just like those who have gone before us.

mots.sens: The word 'Dishon' means 'the serpent' or 'he who is cunning.' It is derived from the Hebrew root that evokes cunning and deception. In the context of genealogy, it represents a lineage that may have implications for the character and actions of the descendants. Spiritually, this reminds us that human nature is often prone to cunning and sin, necessitating redemption in Christ.

The name 'Hamran' can be interpreted as 'the strong' or 'the mighty.' This term evokes notions of strength and robustness, suggesting a personality or lineage marked by power. In the context of genealogy, this can symbolize the strength that God grants to those who are faithful to Him, emphasizing the importance of faith and spiritual strength in the Christian life.

The word 'Eshban' is often interpreted as 'the house of shadow' or 'the refuge.' This can evoke themes of protection and security. In a spiritual sense, this reminds us that God is our refuge and strength, and that we can find peace in Him, even amid life's challenges.

The name 'Jithran' can be understood as 'he who is exalted' or 'he who is lifted up.' This refers to the idea of dignity and high status, symbolizing the spiritual elevation that God grants to those who walk in His ways. This reminds us that our value and identity are in Christ, who lifts us above our circumstances.

41.epoque: This verse is set in the context of the historical chronicles of the people of Israel, likely during a post-exilic period when identity and lineage were crucial for God's people.
41.passage: This passage is part of a genealogy tracing the descendants of Ana, highlighting the importance of lineage in Israel's history. These verses may seem dry, but they are essential for understanding the roots and heritage of God's people.
41.culture: In Hebrew culture, genealogy was a fundamental element of national and spiritual identity. Lineages were carefully recorded to maintain the continuity of God's promises to His people.
41.interpretation: Spiritually, this passage reminds us that each name and each lineage has significance in God's plan. Although these verses may appear obscure, they testify to God's faithfulness through the generations and His commitment to His people.
41.commentaire: This verse, though simple, reminds us that God knows each of us by our name and our story. In our daily lives, we must remember that our identity is rooted in Christ, and that, just like these ancestors, we have a role to play in the divine plan. Let us be encouraged to walk faithfully in our spiritual heritage.

mots.sens: This word designates a proper name, often associated with characters in the genealogy of the descendants of Esau. It can be linked to the idea of help or support, which is relevant in the context of family relationships. Spiritually, this reminds us of the importance of family ties and the continuity of faith through generations.

Bilhan is a name that means 'he who is in distress' or 'he who is in trouble.' This name can evoke personal struggles and the necessity of faith to overcome trials. In the context of genealogy, this emphasizes that even within lineages, challenges are present and require divine grace.

Zaavan is a name that can be translated as 'he who is strong' or 'mighty.' This evokes strength and resilience, qualities often necessary in the life of faith. Theologically, this reminds us that our strength comes from God, and that we must rely on Him in our struggles.

Jaakan is a name that means 'he who laments' or 'he who weeps.' This can symbolize moments of sadness and lamentation in life. Spiritually, this reminds us that God is present in our sufferings and that we can always turn to Him in our moments of despair.

42.epoque: This passage is set in the context of Israel's history, after the exodus from Egypt and before the establishment of the kingdom. It is a period of formation and consolidation of the tribes of Israel.
42.passage: 1 Chronicles 1 is part of an extensive genealogy tracing the origins of the Israelites and their ancestors. This chapter aims to establish the identity and legitimacy of God's people through their ancestors.
42.culture: In Hebrew culture, genealogy plays a crucial role in understanding identity and heritage. The names borne by individuals often carry deep meanings that reflect their character or destiny.
42.interpretation: This verse, although it seems simple, underscores the importance of lineages and heritages in faith. Each name mentioned represents a story and a relationship with God, reminding us that our own spiritual heritage is precious.
42.commentaire: This passage invites us to reflect on the importance of our spiritual and family roots. As believers, we are called to pass on our faith to future generations, just as these ancestors were witnesses to God's faithfulness. Let us take the time to pray for our families and encourage them in their walk with the Lord.

mots.sens: The word 'Edom' means 'red' and is often associated with Esau, the brother of Jacob, who sold his birthright for a bowl of lentils. Edom represents not only a geographical region but also a lineage that often opposes Israel. Spiritually, Edom symbolizes the nations that stand against the people of God, reminding believers of the importance of remaining faithful to their spiritual heritage.

The term 'melech' means 'king' and denotes authority and sovereign power. In the biblical context, a king is often seen as a representative of God on earth, tasked with governing justly. This word emphasizes the notion of divine leadership and the responsibility that comes with it, reminding Christians that Christ is our supreme King.

Dinhaba is the name of the city associated with Bela, the king of Edom. The name could be interpreted as 'the house of justice' or 'the place of decision.' This evokes the idea that even in pagan kingdoms, there is a notion of justice, highlighting God's sovereignty over all nations and the importance of a place of governance.

Bela, son of Beor, is a name that can be associated with the idea of 'destruction' or 'annihilation.' In the context of Edom, this may symbolize judgment and the fragility of human kingdoms in the face of divine power. Spiritually, this reminds us that all earthly power is temporary and that only God's reign is eternal.

43.epoque: This passage is set in a time prior to the establishment of the Israelite monarchy, when kingdoms were often tribal and regional, particularly in Edom.
43.passage: In this chapter, the author of Chronicles traces the genealogy and history of the nations, emphasizing God's sovereignty over the kingdoms and their succession. This verse introduces important figures in the history of Edom, before the people of Israel are established as a nation.
43.culture: The culture of the time valued royal lineages and stories of conquests, which explains why the text mentions the kings of Edom before Israel. It also reflects the historical rivalry between Edom and Israel.
43.interpretation: This verse reminds us that the history of humanity is marked by God's sovereignty, who establishes and overturns kingdoms according to His purpose. It teaches us that even nations that seem prosperous are not above divine judgment.
43.commentaire: This passage encourages us to recognize God's sovereignty in history and in our own lives. As we see kings and kingdoms rise and fall, we must remember that our true King, Jesus Christ, reigns eternally. As believers, we are called to live under His authority and to testify to His power in a world that seeks temporary leaders and solutions.

mots.sens: The name Béla means 'destruction' or 'annihilation.' It is derived from the Hebrew root that evokes the idea of losing or destroying. In the context of this verse, the death of Béla symbolizes the end of a lineage or reign, thus highlighting the fragility of human life and the passage of time. Theologically, this reminds us that even the powerful are subject to mortality and God's sovereignty.

Jobab means 'the one who returns' or 'the one who is restored.' This name may suggest an idea of restoration or renewal, which is relevant in the context of the change of reign. As the successor of Béla, Jobab represents continuity in leadership, but also a new beginning for the people. Spiritually, this teaches us that God can raise new leaders to guide His people in times of transition.

Zérach means 'rising sun' or 'brilliant.' This name evokes light and can symbolize glory or divine favor. In the context of Jobab, son of Zérach, this may indicate that this new king is destined to bring an era of prosperity or spiritual light to the people. This reminds us that God raises leaders who can bring hope and direction.

Botsra means 'vineyard' or 'place of harvest.' This name may have connotations of fertility and prosperity. As the city of origin for Jobab, this suggests that his reign could be associated with blessings and a period of growth for the people. Theologically, this reminds us that God desires for His people to be in a place of blessing and spiritual prosperity.

44.epoque: This verse is set in the context of the Old Testament, during a time when kingdoms and lineages were often marked by power struggles and transitions of leadership.
44.passage: This passage is part of a genealogy in 1 Chronicles, which traces the lineages of the descendants of Israel. It highlights the continuity of kings and leaders within the people of God.
44.culture: In ancient culture, succession to the throne was often determined by lineage and merit, and the death of a king was a crucial moment that could lead to significant changes in the direction of a people.
44.interpretation: The death of Béla and the rise of Jobab illustrate the cycle of life and God's sovereign plan in history. Each change of reign is an opportunity for God to manifest His will and guide His people toward a better future.
44.commentaire: This verse reminds us that life is ephemeral and that each generation must face transitions. As believers, we must prepare for these changes by remaining faithful to God and seeking His direction in our lives. The succession of Jobab after Béla encourages us to see each new step as an opportunity for renewal and divine blessing.

mots.sens: The name Jobab means 'the one who returns' or 'the one who is restored.' In the context of the genealogy of kings, Jobab represents continuity in the royal lineage, emphasizing the importance of succession and stability in leadership. Spiritually, this may evoke the idea of redemption and restoration, central themes in the Christian faith.

Huscham, whose name can be interpreted as 'the one who is strong' or 'the one who is swift,' represents a new king who takes over after Jobab. This underscores the change of leadership and the necessity for strength and swiftness in governance. Theologically, this can symbolize God's providence in establishing leaders according to His plan.

The term Thémanites refers to a group or geographical region, often associated with wisdom and prosperity. In this passage, it indicates the origin of the new king, Huscham, and highlights the importance of alliances and cultural influences in leadership. It can also remind believers of the importance of surrounding themselves with wisdom in their decisions.

45.epoque: This verse is set in an ancient period, likely during the time of the kings of Israel, when dynasties and royal lineages were crucial for the political and social stability of surrounding nations.
45.passage: This passage is part of a genealogy that traces the descendants of Abraham and the kingdoms that arose from them. It highlights the succession of kings and the importance of continuity in leadership.
45.culture: In the culture of the time, succession to the throne was often determined by lineage and alliances between different tribes and nations. The names of kings and their geographical origins were significant in establishing their legitimacy.
45.interpretation: This verse illustrates the transition of power between two kings, highlighting the fragility of human life and the importance of divine sovereignty in the choice of leaders. Spiritually, this reminds us that God is at work in every change of leadership, even when it seems trivial.
45.commentaire: The death of Jobab and the rise of Huscham remind us that each generation must face changes and transitions. As believers, we must rely on divine wisdom to navigate these periods of change. It also encourages us to pray for our leaders, that they may be guided by God's strength and wisdom in their decisions.

mots.sens: The name Husham means 'one who is safe' or 'protection'. This term evokes the idea of refuge and safety, which can be interpreted as divine protection. In the context of the succession of kings, it reminds us that even in transitions of power, God remains the guarantor of His people's safety.

Hadad is a name that means 'thunder'. In Canaanite culture, Hadad was the god of storm and fertility. Spiritually, this name can symbolize power and authority, emphasizing that royalty is under divine authority, and that the victories of kings are manifestations of God's sovereignty over the nations.

Midian refers to the region and the people who were often in conflict with Israel. This term is laden with history, representing opponents to God's will for His people. The mention of the defeat of Midian by Hadad highlights God's victory over the enemies of His people and the fulfillment of His promises.

Avith is the name of a city, which can be interpreted as 'my house'. This evokes the idea of a place of belonging and safety. In the context of royalty, it reminds us that each king has a place of authority and governance, and it can be seen as a metaphor for the spiritual house that God prepares for His people.

46.epoque: This passage is set during the time of the kings of Israel and Judah, a period marked by political struggles and conflicts between nations.
46.passage: In this chapter, the genealogy of the descendants of Israel is presented, highlighting the royal lineages and the transitions of power that occur under God's sovereignty.
46.culture: The culture of the time was heavily influenced by polytheistic beliefs, with kings often associated with deities. Military conquests were seen as manifestations of divine favor.
46.interpretation: This verse illustrates God's sovereignty in the affairs of men, showing that even transitions of power are orchestrated by Him. Hadad's victory over Midian is an image of the struggle between good and evil, where God ultimately triumphs.
46.commentaire: This passage reminds us that God is in control of history, even when changes in leadership occur. As believers, we can trust that God directs our lives and circumstances, and that, like Hadad, we are called to overcome the challenges that stand in our way, supported by divine power.

mots.sens: This name, which means 'thunder', is associated with a storm god in surrounding cultures. In the biblical context, Hadad represents pagan kingdoms and their influence over Israel. The death of Hadad symbolizes the end of an era of power, highlighting God's sovereignty over nations and rulers.

The name Samla is often interpreted as 'one who is reigning'. This term evokes the idea of leadership and continuity in power. In this verse, Samla's reign after Hadad's death can be seen as a divine transition, showing that God directs history even through pagan rulers.

Masréka is a locality mentioned in the Bible, and its name can mean 'place of harvest'. This could symbolize prosperity or abundance. The fact that Samla, from Masréka, reigns indicates that regions considered peripheral can have a significant impact on the course of history.

47.epoque: This verse is set in a period where the surrounding kingdoms of Israel were in constant fluctuation, and where leaders often changed due to wars and conquests.
47.passage: 1 Chronicles 1 is part of a genealogy that traces the origins of peoples and kingdoms, emphasizing God's sovereignty over human history and His plan for Israel.
47.culture: At this time, the neighboring kingdoms of Israel, often at war, had dynamic power systems, where the death of a king often led to succession struggles and significant changes in regional politics.
47.interpretation: The death of Hadad and the rise of Samla illustrate the reality that God is sovereign over nations, even those that seem distant from His people. This reminds us that even in transitions of power, God has a plan and control over history.
47.commentaire: This verse teaches us that every change in leadership, even among pagan nations, is under God's control. This encourages us to trust in His sovereignty in our own lives, knowing that He directs our paths and circumstances. As believers, we must remain steadfast in our faith, even when the world around us changes.

mots.sens: This name means 'to hear' or 'to listen'. In the context of this verse, it evokes the idea of a transition of power, highlighting the importance of the voice of the people and divine will in the choice of leaders. The root of this word is related to perception and receptivity, which can be understood as a call to listen to God's direction in our lives.

The name 'Saul' means 'asked for' or 'lent'. This term emphasizes that Saul was chosen by the people to be their king, raising questions about human expectations versus divine will. Saul also represents the challenges and dangers of leadership, as he will later face spiritual failures.

This term translates to 'wide spaces' or 'openings'. It symbolizes possibilities and opportunities, suggesting that Saul's reign could be marked by expansion and prosperity. Spiritually, this can be seen as an invitation to seek the wide paths that God has prepared for us.

48.epoque: This passage is set in a transitional period for the people of Israel, as they move from a theocracy to a monarchy, seeking a king to govern them like the other nations.
48.passage: 1 Chronicles 1 focuses on genealogies and lineages, establishing a historical context for Saul's reign. This verse marks the beginning of a new era for Israel under the leadership of a human king.
48.culture: In ancient Israelite culture, the choice of a king was a communal and spiritual act, where the people sought God's will. The reign was often perceived as an extension of divine authority on earth.
48.interpretation: The passage emphasizes the importance of succession and continuity in leadership. Spiritually, it reminds us that God is sovereign in the choice of leaders and that He uses circumstances to fulfill His plan.
48.commentaire: This verse teaches us that leadership is a gift from God and must be exercised with wisdom and responsibility. As believers, we are called to pray for our leaders and seek God's will in our own lives, being attentive to His voice that guides us in the choices we make.

mots.sens: The name 'Sha'ul' means 'asked for' or 'borrowed'. It evokes the fact that Saul was chosen by the people of Israel to be king, a request made to God. This name emphasizes the idea that divine leadership is often a response to human request, but it also reminds us of the consequences of a choice that does not always align with God's will.

The name 'Baal-Hanan' can be translated as 'Lord of grace'. This name evokes a notion of kindness and divine favor. In the context of succession to the throne, it underscores the importance of grace in leadership, and how a king must be an instrument of God's goodness toward his people.

The word 'met' means 'to die'. It represents the final term of human life, marking the end of an era. In this verse, the death of Saul is a crucial turning point that reminds us of the fragility of life and the importance of living according to God's ways, as the consequences of our choices can endure beyond our existence.

The verb 'malak' means 'to reign' or 'to govern'. It implies the idea of exercising authority and leading a people. In this context, it highlights the continuity of leadership in Israel, but also the responsibility that each king has to lead the people according to divine principles.

49.epoque: This verse is set in a transitional period for Israel, marked by the end of Saul's reign and the beginning of a new era under Baal-Hanan. It is a time when the people must face the consequences of their political and spiritual choices.
49.passage: The passage focuses on the succession to the throne after the death of Saul, emphasizing the importance of continuity of leadership among the people of Israel. This chapter highlights the dynamics of power and the spiritual implications of the choices made by the people.
49.culture: In Israelite culture, royalty was perceived as a divine mandate, and each king was expected to be in accordance with God's will. The death of a king and the rise of a new sovereign were significant events, often interpreted as signs of divine favor or judgment.
49.interpretation: The death of Saul and the rise of Baal-Hanan illustrate God's sovereignty over the history of Israel. This reminds us that even in difficult transitions, God has a plan and direction for His people, and that each leader must seek divine wisdom in their governance.
49.commentaire: This verse teaches us the importance of dependence on God in leadership. Just as Baal-Hanan took over after Saul, we must remember that each generation must rise to lead according to God's principles. May our lives reflect His grace, and may we always seek to honor God in our responsibilities, whether great or small.

mots.sens: The name 'Baal-Hanan' means 'Lord of grace' or 'Master of grace'. It is composed of 'Baal', which denotes a lord or master, and 'Hanan', which means grace or mercy. This name evokes a certain divine authority and reminds us that even human leaders can be instruments of God's grace in history.

The name 'Hadad' is often associated with a storm god in Canaanite mythology, symbolizing power and strength. In this context, Hadad represents a change of power, highlighting the fragility of human kingdoms in the face of divine sovereignty. Spiritually, this reminds us that God is the true sovereign above all authorities.

The term 'Pahi' designates a city, but its etymology is not entirely clear. In context, it may symbolize a place of refuge or security. This underscores the importance of places in biblical history, where each city can be a symbol of identity and divine protection for its people.

The name 'Mehéthabeel' means 'One who is given by God'. This name emphasizes divine providence in human relationships and the importance of recognizing that everything we have comes from God. It also recalls the idea that unions and families are under divine blessing.

50.epoque: This passage is set in a period of Israel's history where neighboring kingdoms were in constant struggle for power, and dynasties were rapidly succeeding one another.
50.passage: In 1 Chronicles 1, the chapter presents the genealogies and lineages of the descendants of Israel, highlighting the importance of continuity and heritage among the people of God.
50.culture: The culture of the time valued lineages and names, each name having a deep significance that could influence the identity and destiny of individuals and families.
50.interpretation: This verse shows the succession of authority and reminds us that God is sovereign over the events of history, even through figures who may seem distant from His will. The mention of names also emphasizes the importance of faithfulness and grace in the continuity of generations.
50.commentaire: This passage teaches us that even in changes of leadership and struggles for power, God remains in control. It is essential to recognize God's grace in our lives and to understand that every relationship and union is a gift of His providence. As believers, we must remember that our identity and security rest on God's sovereignty, who guides our history.

mots.sens: The word 'Adam' means 'man' or 'humanity' in Hebrew. It is derived from the root 'אדמה' (adamah) which means 'earth', thus highlighting the connection between humanity and creation. In this verse, although 'Hadad' is mentioned, the connection with 'Adam' may remind us of the human condition and mortality, illustrating that even powerful leaders are not exempt from death.

Edom means 'red' in Hebrew, often associated with Esau, the brother of Jacob. This term also evokes the descendants of Esau and his heritage. In this verse, the mention of the chiefs of Edom underscores the importance of this nation in the biblical narrative, often representing opposition to Israel and the consequences of sin.

The term 'Nasi' translates as 'chief' or 'prince', indicating a position of leadership and authority in society. In the context of Edom, these chiefs represent not only political leaders but also figures who have spiritual influence over their people. Their mention after the death of Hadad underscores the continuity of leadership despite mortality.

The word 'Mavet' means 'death' in Hebrew, and it is often used in the Bible to describe spiritual and physical separation. In the context of this verse, the death of Hadad reminds us of the fragility of human life and the inevitable reality of mortality, thus highlighting the necessity of living in accordance with God's ways.

51.epoque: This passage is set in an ancient period, probably during the time of the kingdoms of Israel and Edom, where relations between these nations were marked by conflicts and fluctuating alliances.
51.passage: Chapter 1 of Chronicles traces the genealogy and history of the descendants of Israel, highlighting the lineages and surrounding nations. The mention of the death of Hadad and the chiefs of Edom underscores the continuity of historical events and their impact on the people of Israel.
51.culture: In ancient culture, the death of a leader was a significant event, often accompanied by political changes. The chiefs mentioned here represent figures of power who, although human, play a crucial role in guiding their people.
51.interpretation: The death of Hadad and the list of chiefs of Edom illustrate the reality of mortality and the succession of leaders. Spiritually, this reminds us that earthly kingdoms are temporary, and God's sovereignty prevails over all nations.
51.commentaire: This verse teaches us the importance of recognizing our mortality and living in accordance with divine principles. Like the chiefs of Edom, we have a responsibility toward our community, but we must also remember that our true legacy is found in Christ, who overcomes death. Thus, let us live each day with the wisdom of those who know their time is limited.

mots.sens: This name means 'tent of the height' or 'my tent is elevated.' It evokes the notion of refuge and safety, while being associated with themes of royalty and nobility. In the context of this verse, Oholibamah is a leader among the descendants of Esau, highlighting the importance of lineages and leaders in the history of Israel.

This name means 'oak' or 'tree.' It symbolizes strength, stability, and longevity. In biblical culture, trees are often symbols of life and prosperity, and the name Ela may suggest a certain solidity and authority within the lineage of Esau.

This name is derived from a root that means 'flow' or 'stream.' It can be interpreted as a reference to fertility or prosperity. Spiritually, it may evoke the idea that those who are in Christ are called to be sources of life and blessing for others.

52.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the patriarchal era, where family lineages and tribal leaders were of paramount importance for the survival and identity of peoples.
52.passage: In 1 Chronicles 1, the chapter traces the genealogy of Esau and his descendants, highlighting the leaders who emerged from his lineage. This verse specifically mentions three leaders, shedding light on the social and political organization of these tribes.
52.culture: In ancient culture, the names of leaders and lineages often carried deep meanings and historical narratives. The mention of leaders in this context indicates a well-defined social structure and hierarchy within the tribes.
52.interpretation: Spiritually, this verse reminds us that God has a plan for each generation and that even lineages that seem distant from the promise can have a role in divine history. The leaders mentioned here are witnesses to God's faithfulness to His promises.
52.commentaire: This passage teaches us the importance of knowing our roots and recognizing the role that each generation plays in God's plan. As believers, we are called to be spiritual leaders in our own context, guiding others toward Christ and living in a way that honors our spiritual heritage.

mots.sens: This name means 'spear' or 'protection.' It is associated with a clan leader, emphasizing the importance of leadership and bravery in Israelite culture. The root of this word also evokes notions of strength and defense, which can be interpreted as an image of Christ, our spiritual protector and defender.

The term 'Théman' means 'right' or 'south.' It is often used to designate a geographical direction, but here it can also symbolize the righteousness and integrity of the mentioned leaders. This reminds believers of the importance of walking in justice and truth, following the example of Christ.

This word means 'fortress' or 'bastion.' It evokes the idea of security and refuge, which is essential for understanding the role of leaders in protecting their people. Spiritually, it reminds us that Christ is our fortress, our refuge in times of trouble.

53.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the history of Israel, after the conquest of the promised land, when the tribes are settling and leaders are appointed to guide the people.
53.passage: In 1 Chronicles 1, the chapter presents the genealogy of Israel, highlighting the importance of lineages and leaders who have shaped the history of God's people.
53.culture: Israelite culture valued leadership and bravery, and leaders were often military and spiritual figures who guided the people in battles and in faith.
53.interpretation: These leaders represent essential qualities for the people of God: strength, righteousness, and protection. They are foreshadowings of Christ, who is our supreme leader and defender.
53.commentaire: This verse reminds us of the importance of good direction and leadership in our lives. As believers, we are called to follow the model of Christ, our protector and guide. This encourages us to seek leaders who embody justice and spiritual strength, while reminding us that our true security is found in Christ.

mots.sens: This name means 'God is great' or 'the greatness of God.' It evokes a notion of divine power and preeminence. In the context of Edom, it may remind us that even among the nations, the greatness of God is recognized, thus highlighting His sovereignty over all nations.

The name Iram can be interpreted as 'height' or 'elevated.' This term may refer to a high position or stature among the leaders of Edom. Spiritually, it may evoke the idea that those in positions of authority must be aware of their responsibility before God.

Edom means 'red,' often associated with Esau, the brother of Jacob. This term represents not only a nation but also a symbol of the rivalry between Jacob and Esau, and by extension, between Israel and the nations. Theologically, this underscores the tensions between the people of God and those who oppose Him.

54.epoque: This verse is set in the historical context of the beginnings of nations, after the patriarchal period, when Edom is already established as a nation in opposition to Israel.
54.passage: This passage is part of a larger genealogy in 1 Chronicles, which aims to establish the lineages and heritages of peoples, highlighting the importance of national and spiritual identity.
54.culture: In ancient culture, names often carried deep meanings and were linked to divine attributes or geographical characteristics. The leaders mentioned here are important figures representing the authority and social structure of Edom.
54.interpretation: Spiritually, this verse reminds us that even the nations outside of Israel have a history and a role in God's plan. It teaches us that God's sovereignty extends to all peoples, and that each is called to recognize His greatness.
54.commentaire: This passage, though brief, invites us to reflect on our own heritage and our position before God. It is essential to remember that our identity in Christ transcends cultural and national boundaries. As believers, we are called to live as witnesses of God's greatness, while recognizing our responsibility toward others, whether they are close or distant.
